# Permit Management Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Permit Management Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 9 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved permit environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available and keep the workshop Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded permit knowledge, the proposed permit, document, case, portal and Teams connections, and channel limits; document blocked paths instead of bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for each declared permit, document, case, portal and review connection with least-privilege references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare facility, coordinator, compliance, counsel and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Permit data ownership | Have the permit owner approve the real register, renewal lead times and regulatory requirement mappings before they replace the fixed synthetic records. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Permit status, renewal lead times and open evidence gaps by facility, as tracked today Establish the current tracking effort and audit-readiness gaps before attributing change to the adapted agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Facility | Permit | Issuing authority | Status | Expiration | Renewal lead time | Open evidence gap | Tracking owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Permit owner | Approve permit sources, renewal-planning scope, escalation routes and success measures; retain every submission, renewal and amendment decision. |
| Legal and regulatory reviewers | Validate the obligations behind gap findings and approve remediation; the agent's triage is not legal advice. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any permit connection is approved. |
| Permit system and connection owners | Approve permit-record, controlled-document, case and authority-portal access; record each connection identity and least-privilege reference. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-01 through -04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject evidence lacking its identifiers or Draft state. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route permit decisions to the authorized owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed before production.
- [ ] The permit owner records how register status, renewal lead times and evidence gaps are tracked today before agreeing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/permit-license-management/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The authentication option, required sign-in and allowed audience are approved for permit records, documents and application status.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/permit-license-management/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/permit-license-management/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/permit-license-management/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/permit-license-management/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Permit Management Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: permit-license-management-rules-and-controls.md
7. Add knowledge: permit-license-management-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_application-status
9. Add skill: aibast_compliance-gaps
10. Add skill: aibast_permit-inventory
11. Add skill: aibast_renewal-calendar
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-01: Facility Manager
15. Pass PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-02: Permit Coordinator
16. Pass PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-03: Compliance Manager
17. Pass PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-04: Environmental Counsel
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-01, PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-02, PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-03, PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If Easy mode is chosen, the source-controlled project uses cli-copilot in the approved environment and stays Draft.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `PermitLicenseManagementAgent` and returns `PRM-6002` and `EXPIRED`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Case passes rest on the deterministic validator; an annotated image is a learner checkpoint, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing permit records, documents or application status. Request only the scopes needed for approved permit sources and actions. Restrict the allowed audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Permit system of record

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit system and connection owners

1. **Bind Permit system of record — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Permit system of record:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Permit system of record:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Permit system of record:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the identifier is absent; never substitute another record. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): State that it is absent; never substitute another record or browse for replacement facts.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint controlled documents

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit system and connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint controlled documents — read:** Add the approved document library as knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint controlled documents:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint controlled documents:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint controlled documents:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Decline renewal and filing; return planning evidence and name the authorized permit staff. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, renewal, filing or case update succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Dynamics 365 case management

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit system and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 case management — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any case-creating workflow behind approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 case management:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 case management:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 case management:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Decline renewal and filing; return planning evidence and name the authorized permit staff. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, renewal, filing or case update succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Approved authority portal connector

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit system and connection owners

1. **Bind Approved authority portal connector — write:** Add a separate authenticated tool gated by authorization, current-state checks and confirmation.

2. **Identity for Approved authority portal connector:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved authority portal connector:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved authority portal connector:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Decline renewal and filing; return planning evidence and name the authorized permit staff. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, renewal, filing or case update succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams authorized review

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit system and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams authorized review — read-write:** Gate handoff or approval workflows behind explicit approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams authorized review:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams authorized review:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams authorized review:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Never represent approval; keep the recorded expired status and name the authorized reviewer. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return review evidence and name the authorized reviewer; a future write needs authorization, current-state validation, confirmation and immutable audit logging.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit system and connection owners

Bind least-privilege read connectors first; keep any authority-portal write separate from analysis, confirmed by an authorized role and audited.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no live lookup or update is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Read tools come first; any write stays isolated behind authorization, current-state validation, confirmation and immutable audit logging.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended permit users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user connection access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The permit owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic dates, counts and statuses are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations identify the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked permit corpus | All four cases, PERMIT_LICENSE_MANAGEMENT-01 through -04, return every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Filing authority boundary | Any submission, renewal, amendment, withdrawal or approval claim is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Permit owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved permit audience and supported channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review permit session transcripts, failed interactions, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
